subject: HorizonAI renewal + capacity uplift — pricing & price-hold options
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@horizon.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@horizon.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation — want to align on discount/credits if we bump capacity

Marcus —

Hope you had a good weekend. Our renewal for the pilot seats comes up in July and our usage has ramped faster than expected. We're looking at a ~2.4x capacity uplift across inference usage and would like to understand how Redwood would price that on renewal. Two items we care about: (1) a short-term price hold for the first 90 days while we migrate traffic and (2) some form of one-time credit to offset the delta from our existing commit.

Can you send across a few options (12 vs 24 month commit, any stepped discount tiers, and the mechanics for a price hold)? Procurement wants to see a clean SOW and line-item pricing. Claire is looped to help with requirements.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Khan
Director, Infrastructure & ML Ops
HorizonAI
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@horizon.ai>
Cc: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@horizon.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — want to align on discount/credits if we bump capacity

Samir —

Thanks for the context. We're glad to see the ramp. I've attached a draft SOW and a pricing model (spreadsheet) with three options:

- Option A: 12-month renewal, 15% standard renewal discount, one-time credit equivalent to 10% of the incremental first-year commit, 90-day price hold on per-token rates.
- Option B: 24-month renewal, 18% discount, one-time credit at 12% of incremental commit, 120-day price hold + staged step-down after month 4.
- Option C: Pay-as-you-go with a committed cushion (no long-term discount) + burst pool — for teams that want flexibility while still reserving capacity.

Notes: credits are applied as an invoice credit on the first post-renewal invoice and are not refundable. The price-hold is a contractual cap on the per-token rate for the defined period and does not apply to usage outside agreed model families.

Looped in Laura (Customer Success) to ensure we've modeled the migration window correctly, and Priya from Finance to confirm operational treatment of credits and SOW language.

I'll follow up with a concise summary we can pass to procurement.

Cheers,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Horizon_Renewal_SOW_v2.pdf (PDF, 256 KB)]
[Attachment: renewal_pricing_model_v3.xlsx (XLSX, 42 KB)]
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir@horizon.ai>, Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@horizon.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — want to align on discount/credits if we bump capacity

Team — quick notes from Finance after a first pass on Marcus's options: 

- We can validate Option A/Option B structure but need to be explicit about the credit amortization (we prefer one-time invoice credit vs multi-invoice amortization). Samir: confirm procurement preference.
- For price-hold: we're comfortable with a 90–120 day cap but will need a clear definition of which model families and token classes are covered. 
- If Horizon wants the credit to cover true-up exposure for the migration period, we should add a capped true-up clause (max X% of incremental usage) to limit outsized exposure.

Also: procurement typically asks for a separate line in the SOW for burst/overage billing mechanics to avoid confusion. Marcus, can you add a short section that shows how we fallback to pay-as-you-go for any usage above the committed cushion?

Priya Natarajan
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@horizon.ai>, Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@horizon.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 May 2028 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — want to align on discount/credits if we bump capacity

Samir / Claire —

Thanks for the quick responses. Per Priya's ask, I've updated the SOW to include: (a) a standalone burst/overage line showing PAYG rates, (b) a clause that the credit is a single invoice credit applied on the first invoice post-renewal, and (c) a capped migration true-up (we propose cap = 25% of the incremental commit for the first 60 days).

To be explicit on numbers (Option A example):
- Current commit: 1.0M tokens/month
- Proposed commit: 2.4M tokens/month (24 month look: 28.8M annual)
- Incremental first-year commit = (2.4 - 1.0) * 12 = 16.8M tokens
- One-time credit (10%) = credit equal to 1.68M tokens @ list rate applied as invoice credit (we'll show USD equivalent on the pricing sheet)
- Price hold = cap on per-token list rate for 90 days from renewal effective date

Next steps: if Horizon is comfortable, we can convert Option A to a redlineable addendum and send to procurement. If you're leaning toward a 24-month term, we'll floor the discount at 18% and extend price-hold to 120 days.

Available to hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the SOW line-by-line.

Best,
Marcus
From: Samir Khan <samir@horizon.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@horizon.ai>, Procurement <procurement@horizon.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — want to align on discount/credits if we bump capacity

Marcus / team —

Thanks — this is helpful and very clear. Procurement prefers the one-time invoice credit approach. We're inclined to accept Option A with the 90-day price hold provided the SOW defines the covered model families (we'll cross-check with our ML team). A couple of asks before we route to legal: 

1) Can Redwood confirm the USD value of the 10% credit on the attached spreadsheet and show it as a line-item credit on page 2?
2) We'd like a short clause that the price-hold cannot be invoked to reduce an existing committed rate below what's already paid (i.e., no retroactive downward adjustments).
3) Can you add a 30-day early-exit clause tied to material SLA breaches for the first 90 days (procurement's standard ask for migrations)?

If those three items are addressed, procurement will take the redline and push to legal. Happy to take the 30min call Monday to finalize any language.

Samir
